question: Should Microsoft Teams permanently adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus `defaultAccount`, with root settings inherited by named accounts and legacy root credentials treated as the default account?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but it creates a durable public configuration, credential-selection, and persisted-state contract whose acceptance cannot be inferred from tests or CI.

options.title: Sponsor the account contract
options.body: Approve the proposed account, inheritance, and legacy rules; require final current-main and security-owner review; then merge.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Keep the feature but ask the contributor to reduce inheritance or legacy behavior before accepting the public configuration shape.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Close the PR and linked direction if maintainers do not want multiple Teams bot identities in the official plugin.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the account contract
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed account, inheritance, and legacy rules; require final current-main and security-owner review; then merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This cross-cutting product and configuration compatibility decision needs repository-level ownership, and @steipete is the strongest owner identified by policy and ownership evidence.
